newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Moslem gathering in Bangladesh calls for peace.
newsitem.headline: Moslem gathering in Bangladesh calls for peace.

text.p: An estimated two million Moslems from around the world wound up a three-day annual gathering on Monday with mass prayers calling for peace through the practising of Islamic tenets, organisers said.
Islamic scholars urged devotees to shun luxuries, follow the teachings of Islam and seek blessings from Allah.

Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her arch rival Begum Khaleda Zia, chief of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party, attended the annual ceremony at Tongi, 18 km (12 miles) north of Dhaka.

Held on the bank of river Turag, the event, called Biswa Ijtema, drew Moslems from more than 70 countries, including Britain, the United States, France, Germany, China, India and most Moslem nations, organisers said.
Nearly 80 couples were married at the Ijtema, which is believed to have been held at the same venue for more than 100 years.
